I've not tested the claim of 48 lbs of ice in a day, largely because I haven't had the need for 48 lbs of ice at one time for quite a while, but I'm pretty sure that if you had a separate freezer to store the ice and someone that was monitoring the thing continually, you'd be able to get more than 35 lbs in a day. Downside is that it's not really capable of being plumbed in, so you have to manually refill the water reservoir.

This ice make stopped working after about 10 months of daily use, far too short a life for such an expensive appliance, hence the 1-star review. Unfortunately nearly all the competing models of this capacity seem to be of near-identical design.

Until it died, I overall liked this ice maker. Some other comments about it:
- It makes ice quickly, but can only hold a moderate amount (2.3 lbs?), which is fine if you are emptying it regularly, but filling a large bag or cooler would take constant emptying all day.
- The cubes come out frozen but melt as they sit in the collection basket and so are are cold but a bit "melty".overall. They're not nearly as cold or hard as the cubes from my freezer's icemaker.
- This means they melt and dilute your drinks quicker, if that matters to you. It also means if you put them in a freezer to refreeze them, them tend to stick together..
- The ice maker itself can be quite noisy at times. Not just the clatter of ice as it is dumped but occasional assorted whines, groans, wheezes and whirs as it makes the ice, sometimes load enough to be heard at the far end of my house from the ice maker.
- We like to use filtered water for the ice maker. The PUR 18-cup dispenser/filter matches the capacity of the ice maker and works well for us.
- The temperature range the ice maker allows is quite limited, IIRC, about 50-86 degrees.
- This sucker is pretty big. It barely fits under the upper cabinet

Great Ice Maker - I had a smaller ice maker that made about 26lbs of Ice daily and had 2 size of ice cubes but did not seem to do what I needed so I thought I would try Ivation 48-pound Daily Capacity Counter Top Ice Maker and this baby put out the ice. You just plug it in pour water in the reservoir set the size of ice cube you want and turn it on it's just that easy. It has a water level indicator light and alert to let you know that the water is low. The unit shuts off automatically when the ice bucket is full for safety.

I live in a rental and my refrigerator does not have an ice maker. Ive been shopping around for a while now on a portable ice maker, that way I can take it with me when I move. This ice maker is much bigger than I expected. However, it is very well made and was shipped very well to make sure it received no damage. Ive made 5 cycles of ice now and so far so good!! I like that I can select the ice size and have tried all 3 sizes but find the medium size works best for my family. I was surprised how quickly this machine made ice! Overall, it's not as noisy as I expected either. My only complaint is that it does not keep the ice cold once the ice is made. I have to make sure I am paying attention to when it's done so I can transfer the ice to my freezer bucket before it melts. I am happy with this product.

A lot bigger than I expected!  Was very happy with that.  Your instructions are very self explanatory.  Ice maker can yield 48 pounds plus a day if you keep refilling it.  There are 3 different ice cube sizes, and the ice is the round kind with the hole in the end.  Makes very soft, easy to crunch ice.  The soft ice is my absolute favorite and that's what this makes.  Be sure that when you first get your ice maker you wait at least 30 minutes to plug it in, as it needs to settle in case it was turned upside down or shaken during delivery.  You are going to want to wipe down the inside really good with some vinegar to get the "new plastic" smell out of it and let it air out a bit.  If you don't your ice will have a bad taste and smell to it.  Let a few cycles run through as well and dump out the ice.  You can fill it with your tap water or purified bottled water if you choose.  The ice will have a different texture and will be harder if you use the purified water.  I tried a gallon of "bought water" and it was clear and hard.  The water from my tap was white and soft.  I suppose it has something to do with the oxygen in the different types of water.  Nevertheless this is a good sized ice maker.  The ice dumps in the basket and keeps it cool pretty long.  Once it melts it just drops back into the water reservoir and is recycled back into making ice.

I left the power on over night and it was filled to the brim with ice the next day. This is a feature I really enjoy. I used distilled water in the reservoir and the ice turned out crystal clear.

The first 2 batches are small (even on the large setting) because the rods aren't cold yet, so we just dump them back into the water reservoir.  Used this to make ice for a couple parties - As long as you have plastic bags & freezer space to make ahead of time & store, it's great!
